facts.claim: On the first of September Arjun wrote to Ravi that Nimbus Labs is raising a seed round to bring calendar-aware planning to small teams, and asked for twenty minutes the following week.
facts.quote: Ravi, Nimbus Labs is raising a seed round to bring calendar-aware planning to small

facts.claim: On the third Ravi Iyer of Seedfund Partners answered, thanking him and asking for the deck before they speak.
facts.quote: deck before we speak? Ravi Iyer Seedfund Partners

facts.claim: Ravi's ask is open and waits on us, and the file names the move as ours.
Since Ravi's mail the file has been quiet for over a week, longer than any gap it closed before.
The brief names no kind of work for Seedfund; the engine filed it as an investor relationship under fundraising.

inferences.claim: Ravi agreed to talk on one condition, the deck first: the meeting Arjun asked for now waits only on Arjun.
The longer the deck waits, the more the investor's interest cools.

hypotheses.proposition: Ravi's answer reached a different mailbox from the one the pitch went out of, and the founder has not seen it.
hypotheses.needs: The founder's word on whether he saw Ravi's mail of the third.

unknowns.question: Whether the founder has seen Ravi's mail of the third.
unknowns.relevance: If he missed it, the delay is an oversight to fix at once; if he saw it, something is holding the deck back.

unknowns.question: Whether the deck is ready to share.
unknowns.relevance: Ravi asked for it before the call; without it the meeting waits.

unknowns.question: Who Ravi is at Seedfund Partners and the size of its seed cheques.
unknowns.relevance: It decides how much of the round this conversation can carry.

frames.primary: An investor agreed to talk and asked for the deck first; the deck has not gone, and the move has been ours for over a week.
rivals: The founder missed Ravi's answer because it reached a different mailbox from the pitch.
The deck went by another channel the file cannot see.

proposed_kind.why: Arjun pitched Nimbus Labs' seed round to Ravi, and Ravi answers for Seedfund Partners asking for the deck before a call — an investor conversation, which the engine already files under fundraising.

expected_vs_actual.expected: Without a playbook, the thread sets it: Ravi asked for the deck before speaking, so the deck was due promptly, with a time for the call.
expected_vs_actual.actual: No deck has gone as far as the file shows, and it has been quiet for over a week since his mail.

scenarios.do_nothing: Ravi's interest cools, the meeting you asked for is never booked, and Seedfund drops out of the round without saying so.
scenarios.act: The deck reaches Ravi with an apology for the wait and a request for a time, and the call goes in the calendar.
scenarios.best: Ravi reads the deck, the call is booked, and Seedfund moves toward a partner discussion.
scenarios.worst: The delay reads as a founder not raising in earnest, and Ravi does not take the call.
signals_to_watch: Ravi proposing a time once the deck goes.
Questions from Ravi about the deck.

reasons: Raising the seed round is the brief's first goal, and this investor asked to see the deck before a call.
The move has been ours for over a week, longer than any gap the file closed before.
Momentum lost with an investor is hard to win back.

next_move.what: Reply to Ravi Iyer with your deck, apologise for the wait, and ask which time suits him for the call.

parsed.alternative: If the deck is not ready, reply today saying when it will come, and ask for a time for the call.
parsed.wait_or_stop: Do not wait — the move is ours. After the deck goes, give Ravi a week to propose a time; if nothing comes, send one short note with something new, then stop.
parsed.done_when: Ravi has the deck and a call with him is on the calendar.
parsed.draft: Hi Ravi, thank you for coming back to me, and sorry for the wait. Here is the Nimbus Labs deck. Which time suits you for a call? Arjun
